title: Address Space: Where Your Program Lives in Memory
topic: Address space layout — every process sees a virtual memory region with code at the bottom, static data above it, the heap growing up via malloc, and the stack growing down on each function call

beats.narration: Every program sees a clean slab of memory laid out the same way each time it runs.

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre-screen
Where in memory does each part of your program live?

beats.narration: At the bottom sits your code, frozen and read-only. Above it, the static data the compiler set up. The stack lives at the top — and the heap is everything in between.

elements.content: Vertical address-space rectangle with low addresses at the bottom, high at the top
Code segment block at the bottom
Data segment block above code
Heap label at the bottom of the gap with an upward arrow
Stack label at the top of the gap with a downward arrow
Address axis labels: 0 at bottom, 2^n − 1 at top
code · data · heap · stack — the four neighbourhoods of every process

beats.narration: Call malloc, and the heap creeps upward. Each new block sits wherever the allocator can find room.

elements.content: First malloc — small block appears at the bottom of the heap area
malloc(32) label next to first block
Second malloc — block stacks on top of the first
malloc(64) label next to second block
Third malloc — block stacks again, the heap-top arrow rises
malloc(16) label next to third block
heap-top moves up — toward the stack

beats.narration: Call a function, and a new frame is pushed onto the stack — locals, return address, the works. Return, and the frame is gone.

elements.content: First call — main()'s frame appears at the top of the stack area
main() label inside frame 1
Second call — work()'s frame stacks below
work() label inside frame 2
Third call — helper()'s frame stacks below; stack-top arrow descends
helper() label inside frame 3
helper() returns — frame 3 fades out and stack-top arrow rises back
stack-top moves down — toward the heap

beats.narration: Two arrows, growing toward each other. As long as the gap holds, the program runs.

elements.content: Heap grows up. Stack grows down. They meet — that's out of memory.
